2.1Overview of National Executive

2.1.1
The National Executive is the elected leadership of the FederationCFES and consists of the following five positions:
(a)President
(b)Vice President Academic
(c)Vice President Finance
(d)Vice President External
(e)Vice President Services
(f)Vice President Communications
RewordedBylaws §3.1 Overview of National Executive, cl. 1also amended by ,
2.1.2
The National Executive's general tasks and responsibilities include:
(a)Upholding the Constitution, Bylaws, and Policies of the FederationCFES
(b)Organizing and directing the efforts of the FederationCFES
(c)Ensuring the completion of all mandates
(d)Managing Commissioners within their respective portfolios, and assuming responsibilities in the event they are not completed
(e)Making contact with government bodies when necessary
(f)Hiring working groups for their successors as required by April 30th
(g)Creating a transition document by April 30th to be stored in the electronic CFES archive
RewordedBylaws §3.1 Overview of National Executive, cl. 2Constitution §5.1 Composition, cl. 2also amended by

2.2President

2.2.1
The President’s tasks and responsibilities include:
(a)Providing leadership and oversight for the National Executive
(b)Ensuring the mandates of each Vice President are completed
(c)Organizing meetings of the National Executive
(d)Ensuring that long term planning for the FederationCFES is undertaken, with annual updates given to the Members
(e)Maintaining communication channels with all stakeholders of the FederationCFES
(f)Ensuring communication with Engineers Canada and attending the Engineers Canada Annual General Meeting and Board Meetings, if feasible
RewordedBylaws §3.2 President, cl. 1also amended by

2.7Vice President Communications (VPC)

2.7.1
The VPC’s tasks and responsibilities include:
(a)Maintaining and upkeeping an archive of original files relating to the logo, banners, branded items, and templates of the CFES.
(b)Maintaining and enforcing the logo and branding guidelines of the CFES
(c)Assisting Activities with the creation of design templates for documents or promotional materials, as necessary
(d)Sourcing quotes for branded items for the CFES or its Activities as necessary
(e)Updating social media profiles for the FederationCFES
(f)Directing the Media & Marketing Working Group, which shall make graphics, research trends, and provide new ideas on how to best use the CFES socials.
(g)Directing the Bilingualism Working Group, which shall support translation, make plans to improve bilingualism at Activities or online meetings, and help make bilingualism resources for others.
(h)Facilitating engagement between Members throughout the year.
(i)Sending out publications to the Members every other month to keep them up to date with the progress of the CFES Team.

2.3Regions

2.3.1
–The Federation comprises of 4 regions. They are:
The CFES shall be comprised of four (4) regions, each represented at the national level:
(a)Atlantic – Provinces of Prince Edward Island, of New Brunswick, of Nova Scotia, and of Newfoundland and Labrador;
(b)Quebec – Province of Quebec;
(c)Ontario – Province of Ontario; and
(d)West – Provinces of British Columbia, of Alberta, of Saskatchewan, of Manitoba, and The Territory of Yukon, Territory of Nunavut and North-WestNorthwest Territories.

13MembershipObserver status abolished

Repealed from the current Constitution

§3.3Observer Status

3.3.1
An Observer of the Federation is an Engineering Society which received the support of the Board as specified in the Bylaws.
3.3.2
Observer status is valid for one year after an application is approved after which point the Observer must choose to apply to become a Regular Member as per Article 3.1.2, apply for a one-time extension or withdraw membership both as per the Bylaws.

Repealed from the current Bylaws

§7.2.3Observer

7.2.3.1
An observer does not have voting rights in the Federation.

§7.3.3Application to be granted Observer Status

7.3.3.1
To apply for observer status an organization must submit a written application to the Vice-President Finance and Administration, who must immediately inform the Board of such an application.
7.3.3.2
The Board must then make a decision regarding the organization admission, and this no later than the Board meeting following the organization's submission of the application.
7.3.3.3
Following a decision from the Board, the members shall be immediately notified.
7.3.3.4
A society may only apply for observer status if at any point in the past 12 months they have neither been a regular member nor held observer status.

§7.3.4Application to extend Observer Status

7.3.4.1
An observer may apply for a one-time extension at the end of their first year as an observer.
7.3.4.2
To extend observer an organization must submit a written application to the Vice-President Finance and Administration, who must immediately inform the Board of such an application.
7.3.4.3
The application must include the following:

7Member Discipline

–The Board may, by resolution adopted by two thirds (2/3) of Board present at a meeting convened to this end, suspend any member which infringes upon a resolution or by-law of the Federation or whose conduct or activities are deemed detrimental to the wellbeing or functioning of the Federation, or who has not paid their membership fees for the current year, as outlined in Policy 8.1.1., or who has not paid their delegate fees for an activity..
–A General Assembly may, by resolution adopted by 2/3 of members present at a member's assemble, expel any member which infringes upon the CFES constitution, or whose conduct or activities are deemed detrimental to the wellbeing or functioning of the CFES.

(a)violating any provision of the Articles, Constitution, Bylaws, or Policies of the CFES;
(b)carrying out any conduct which may be detrimental to the CFES as determined by the Board in its sole discretion;
(c)for any other reason that the Board in its sole and absolute discretion considers to be reasonable, having regard to the purpose of the CFES.
RewrittenBylaws §7.3.2 Expulsion of Members, cl. 1Bylaws §7.3.1 Suspension of Members, cl. 1
7.2
–Within two business days after the suspension of a member, the President shall inform all members of the suspension, with reasoning provided.
–A General Assembly may, by resolution adopted by 2/3 of members present at a member's assemble, expel any member which infringes upon the CFES constitution, or whose conduct or activities are deemed detrimental to the wellbeing or functioning of the CFES.
In the event that the Board determines that a Member should be expelled or suspended from membership in the CFES, the Chair shall provide twenty (20) days notice of suspension or expulsion to the Member and shall provide reasons for the proposed suspension or expulsion. The Member may make written submissions to the Chair in response to the notice received within such twenty (20) day period. In the event that no written submissions are received by the Chair, the Chair may proceed to notify the Member that the Member is suspended or expelled from membership in the CFES. If written submissions are received in accordance with this section, the Board will consider such submissions in arriving at a final decision and shall notify the Member concerning such final decision within a further twenty (20) days from the date of receipt of the submissions. The Board's decision shall be final and binding on the Member, without any further right of appeal.

8.7.2.7
Any error or omission in mailing the voting notice of the mail-in ballot will not annul the ballot.
8.7.2.8
The active members will receive the voting notice at their last known address in the books of the Federation.

76ActivitiesIncident Response Committee abolished

70 provisions repealed

Repealed from the current Bylaws

§11.1Purpose

11.1.1
The Incident Reporting Form will be the way that the Incident Response Committee receives complaints of violations of the Code of Conduct.
11.1.2
To ensure that CFES Activities are a safe and welcoming space for everyone, an Incident Response Committee shall be formed to investigate and attempt to resolve any reported issues.
11.1.3
The goal of the Incident Response Committee shall be to ensure that a safe and inclusive environment is maintained at CFES Activities.

§11.2.1Structure

11.2.1.1
The Incident Response Form shall be a form created by the Incident Response Committee and made accessible to all delegates at a CFES Activity during the Activity and up to 3 days afterwards.
11.2.1.2
The form shall include the following fields:
(a)Name of Reporting Individual
(b)School of Reporting Individual
(c)Name(s) of the Individual(s) or Organization Involved in the Incident (or description(s))
(d)Incident Date and Time
(e)Incident Details
(f)Incident Witness(es), if appropriate
(g)Contact Information (Optional)
(h)Whether or not the Reporter is comfortable being contacted by the IRC
(i)A description of any personal relationships or potential conflicts of interest with IRC members, with regards to both the reporting individual or anyone involved in the complaint
(j)A brief description of IRC procedure, which includes clarifying that all complaints submitted through the Incident Reporting Form will go to the Chair of the IRC and that if complainants wish to submit complaints outside of the form, it must be done through the contact information on this form.

§11.2.2Confidentiality of Reports

11.2.2.1
Any identifying contents of Incident Reports, and identifying information discovered during the investigation, shall be kept confidential by the members of the Incident Response Committee (IRC) subject only to Bylaw 10.3.6: Release of Information.

§11.2.3Incident Response Timeline

11.2.3.1
Should a report be submitted between 8am and 8pm, the Incident Response Committee shall begin to address the report within four hours.
11.2.3.2
Should a report be submitted outside of these times, but during the conference, the IRC shall begin to address the report by the following noon.
11.2.3.3
The IRC is not permitted to work through meal time, and thus any report open during that time has its timeline extended.
11.2.3.4
Should a report be submitted with less than 4 hours remaining in the conference, or within 72 hours after midnight of the last day of the conference, the IRC shall begin to address the report within 36 hours.

§11.3.1Structure

11.3.1.1
An Incident Response Committee (IRC) shall be formed for each CFES Activity.

§11.3.2Committee Membership

11.3.2.1
An IRC shall consist of up to six (6) members including:
(a)Up to two non voting members of the Board who shall serve as IRC Chair(s).
(b)The proposed IRC Chair(s) shall be responsible for choosing an IRC committee and presenting it to the Board for approval.
(c)The committee can consist of one or a combination of the following:
i.Four members of the OC, chosen by the Activity Manager(s) with consultation of the Board
A.These OC members can maintain their usual responsibilities if possible
B.A separate OC hire (1-4 individuals) conducted by the Activity Manager(s) can be considered if the Activity Manager(s) expresses reasonable concern over workload.
C.The individuals will be welcome to attend sessions if applicable for the Activity.
ii.Four non-member delegates selected by the Board.
11.3.2.2
CELC may have two separate IRCs, each consisting of an IRC chair and four non-member delegates for a total of 2 IRC chairs and eight non-member delegates.
11.3.2.3
In the case of two IRC chairs, they shall throughout the entirety of the Activity share duties.
11.3.2.4
For each case, only one of the two chairs will act as a voting chair while the other performs as a consultant chair without a vote.
11.3.2.5
The consultant chair may sit in for any interviews and case discussions, but does not have a final vote.
11.3.2.6
Chairs will alternate as voting chairs between cases to balance workload.
11.3.2.7
Co-chairs may distribute cases between them as they see fit.
11.3.2.8
The IRC membership will:
(a)Undergo IRC introductions with the National Councillors
(b)Undergo Psychological First Aid Training paid for by the CFES.
(c)Have no more than one member of the Board.
(d)Be ratified by the Board no later than 2 weeks before the start of the Activity.
(e)Be kept confidential, unless necessary for the IRC to complete their duties, for the duration of the conference
11.3.2.9
When selecting members of the IRC, the Board shall make an effort to ensure that the composition of the IRC reflects a diverse range of perspectives and backgrounds.
11.3.2.10
Additionally, the Board shall make an effort to ensure that members do not serve on multiple consecutive IRCs when possible.
11.3.2.11
To mitigate the psychological risks associated with this role, IRC members will be required to submit emotional safety plans to the Board no later than three (3) days before the beginning of the activity.
11.3.2.12
Emotional safety plans must include, at a minimum, the following;
(a)A recognition of the emotional labour associated with the role and a willingness to participate in such labour
(b)An outline of professional supports available to the IRC member.
(c)An outline of personal supports available to the IRC member.
(d)Contact information for individuals identified by the IRC member as key-emotional supports.
11.3.2.13
In the case of extreme emotional duress, IRC members may use the professional & personal supports outlined in their emotional safety plans to discuss concerns relating to their work as an IRC member.
11.3.2.14
IRC members are not permitted to discuss their role as an IRC member with other attending delegates and are subject to Bylaw 10.3.6 in all other matters relating to their role.
11.3.2.15
The Organizing Committee, with consultation of the IRC and National Executive, is expected to gather mental health resources to have ready for the Activity in order to direct delegates to them for professional support.
11.3.2.16
These can be services offered by the Activity, or external resources that may be offered in the city/province of the Activity.
11.3.2.17
If there are no mental health resources available, the IRC Chair must let the Board know so other precautions can take place.

§11.3.3Committee Authority

11.3.3.1
Decisions made by the IRC shall be considered final for the duration of the Activity, and may range from verbally reprimanding an offending delegate to expulsion from the conference.
11.3.3.2
After the conclusion of the Activity, the respondent may appeal decisions made by the IRC.
11.3.3.3
Delegates may not be expelled by any other authority of the CFES.
11.3.3.4
The IRC may not make decisions that affect the delegate's ability to contribute to the CFES in the future, such as conditionally or completely banning from further conferences, but may recommend these actions to the Appeal Board.

§11.3.4Committee Response Procedure

11.3.4.1
All complaints submitted through the Incident Reporting Form will first be examined by the Chair of the IRC, and the Chair of the IRC will examine the form to determine whether any members of the IRC should not have access to the complaint due to conflict of interest as per Bylaw 10.3.5.
11.3.4.2
Once this is determined, the Chair of the IRC shall share the form responses with all relevant members of the IRC and begin their investigation.
11.3.4.3
If a complaint is submitted to another member of the IRC due to a conflict of interest with the IRC Chair, the member who the complaint was submitted to shall conduct the same process before sharing the complaint with other IRC members.
11.3.4.4
To ensure that the IRC has a complete picture of the Incident, and the impact it has had on the involved parties, they should contact the following parties and discuss the Incident and appropriate responses:
(a)The Respondent(s)
(b)The Affected Person(s)
(c)The individual who made the report, if appropriate
(d)Any witnesses to the Incident, if absolutely necessary
11.3.4.5
Note: The Respondent(s) and the Affected Persons' will be invited to have an additional individual for support present during any conversations.
11.3.4.6
After these discussions, the IRC shall use their best judgment on what response is appropriate or if further investigation is needed.
11.3.4.7
All IRC decisions require a majority vote, and the chair of the IRC shall only vote in the event of a tie.
11.3.4.8
Any official communications should be made by the Chair of the IRC, with the knowledge and approval of all members of the IRC except in cases where the Chair of the IRC has a conflict of interest as described in Bylaw 10.3.5.
11.3.4.9
In this case, the IRC shall appoint one of their members to make official communications for the complaint in question.
11.3.4.10
Responses to any official communication should be shared with all IRC members.
11.3.4.11
The IRC should ensure that there are at least two IRC members present for any conversation with anyone involved with the Incident.
11.3.4.12
The IRC should be directing those involved to the mental health resources mentioned in 8.4.2.4.

§11.3.5Conflict of Interest

11.3.5.1
A conflict of interest shall be defined as a strong positive or negative personal relationship between a member of the IRC and the Respondent, Victim, or other individuals involved in the Incident that unfairly biases their actions or decisions.
11.3.5.2
A member of the IRC should remove themselves from the IRC if they believe they have a perceived or real conflict of interest.
11.3.5.3
Should anyone believe that an IRC member has a conflict of interest, it should be presented to the IRC.
11.3.5.4
If one member of the IRC believes that a perceived or real conflict of interest exists, the appropriate member shall be removed from the IRC.
11.3.5.5
If three or more members of the IRC are required to step down due to conflict of interest, the remaining members of the IRC will be responsible for choosing a replacement member on a temporary or permanent basis, as appropriate, and notifying the Appeal Board of the change.
11.3.5.6
The remaining members of the IRC shall release changes of membership to the Activity delegates if there are permanent changes, and these changes shall be reflected on the Incident Response Form.
11.3.5.7
In the case of two IRC chairs, if one of the chairs has a conflict of interest, the other chair must take over the case without consultation from the other chair.

§11.3.6Release of Information

11.3.6.1
The IRC is expected to keep all identifying information for anyone involved other than the Respondent permanently confidential except in the following situations:
(a)The IRC or anyone involved with the Incident decides that the Police should be notified, or;
(b)The IRC has obtained written consent of everyone involved to release the information.
11.3.6.2
The IRC is expected to keep confidential any information that may identify the Respondent, except in the following situations:
(a)The IRC or anyone involved with the Incident decides that the Police should be notified, or;
(b)The IRC has obtained written consent of everyone involved to release the information, or;
(c)The IRC recommends that the Board notify the Respondent's school i.e. The Dean's office) the nature of the complaint.
11.3.6.3
The IRC recommends that the Board limit or end an individual' s involvement in CFES activities.
11.3.6.4
If the Board (after the appeal has been finalized) decides to uphold this recommendation the member society shall be notified of the individual' s status but not of the reasoning for the decision.
11.3.6.5
Should the IRC decide to take action against a delegate they are to inform the head delegate of the decision.
11.3.6.6
If the action is being taken against a head delegate the delegate' s Regional Ambassador is to be informed.
11.3.6.7
If an IRC member breaches these confidentiality rules, they may be subject to discipline by the Board.

§11.3.7Best Practices

11.3.7.1
The IRC be briefed by the National Councillors on best practises as per the Incident Response Committee Best Practises document.
11.3.7.2
The Incident Response Best Practises should be maintained by the National Executive and IRC Chairs.

§11.4.1Purpose

11.4.1.1
Should anyone feel that a decision made by the Incident Response Committee (IRC), or that the process followed by the IRC, was unfair they may Appeal the decision by informing the IRC Chair.

§11.4.2Appeal Board

11.4.2.1
The Board shall hear all appeals resulting from decisions made by the IRC.
11.4.2.2
Any Board members who were members of the IRC should attend the meeting where an appeal is heard to provide information, but should not participate in any decision made regarding the appeal.
11.4.2.3
The Board may uphold or overturn decisions made by the IRC, and may accept the recommendation of the IRC to limit an individual' s involvement with the CFES for a period of time, or until certain conditions are met.
11.4.2.4
All decisions made by the Board are final.

§11.4.3Appeal Timeline

11.4.3.1
Appeals will be accepted by the IRC Chair for 72 hours after either the close of the Activity, or notice of a decision made by the IRC, whichever happens last.
11.4.3.2
A meeting will be scheduled by the Board Chair 14 days of the Appeal being made to hear from the individual who brings forward the Appeal and, separately, the Chair of the IRC

§11.4.4Conflict of Interest

11.4.4.1
A member of the Board should remove themselves from the Appeal Process if they believe they have conflict of interest as defined in Bylaw 10.3.5.

§11.5Recording of Information

11.5.1
In the case that a school is notified of the IRC's decision, or that a decision to limit or end an individual's involvement is made, the following should be recorded and kept by the National Councillors for future iterations of the IRC:
(a)Name of Respondent.
(b)Decision that was reached.
(c)Relevant copies of correspondence with the School and/or Individual.
11.5.2
Otherwise, the following information should be recorded and kept by the National Councillors for future IRCs:
(a)High level summary of the incident names, schools, or any other identifying information.
(b)Decision that was reached.

–The election procedures outlined in the Policy Manual are valid for the election in the Annual General Meeting or by the Board for the National Councillors and the National Executive.

96ElectionsVoting by instant-runoff

47 changes

Electoral Bylaws

8Voting

8.1
–The election procedures must include a stipulation that, to be elected, a candidate must receive the absolute majority of the vote, abstentions excluded.
–The election must be held by means of a secret ballot.
–To be elected, a candidate must receive the absolute majority of the members voting (50% +1), abstentions excluded.
–Each Member shall submit a ballot comprised of a ranked list of candidates.
–The member is able to rank as many or as few of the candidates as desired.
–For the President, Vice President Academic, Vice President Services, and Vice President Finance & Administration positions: one candidate may be ranked as a first choice.
–Should less than one candidate receive the majority of first-choice votes outright, the single candidate runoff procedure shall be enacted.
–For the National Councillor positions:
–up to two distinct candidates may be ranked equally as first choices.
–One candidate may be ranked for each rank other than first.
–Should fewer than two candidates receive majorities of first-choice votes outright, the dual candidate runoff procedure shall be enacted.
–The current National Executive, excluding any National Executive member who is standing for election, shall submit a ballot comprised of a ranked list of candidates.
–The National Executive must rank all candidates, each receiving a unique rank
–This ballot will only be viewed in the event of a tie, as outlined below.
–The number of first‐choice votes for each candidate is counted.
Voting shall occur by means of secret ballot using a transferable-vote system.
(a)For elections to a single position, the Instant-Runoff Voting (IRV) method shall be used.
–If one candidate has received more than 50% of the vote, this candidate is declared the winner, and the procedure is complete.
i.In the event that no candidate obtains more than 50% of the vote following this procedure, no candidate shall be declared elected or nominated, and a new election may be held.
–In the event that no candidate has received more than 50% of the vote, the candidate who received the lowest number of first choice votes is dropped from the running.
–In the event that two or more candidates are tied in receiving the lowest number of first-place votes, all tied candidates are dropped from the running, except in the case when this would reduce the remaining eligible candidates to zero.
–In such a case, the candidate to be dropped will be the candidate with the lower rank on the National Executive ballot.
–Only one candidate will be dropped in this case.
–On all ballots with the dropped candidate ranked as a first choice, the candidate ranked second on the ballot is treated as having been ranked first, unless the second choice candidate has already been dropped.
–In this case, the next choice will be counted as first, etc.
–The number of first choice votes for each candidate is counted again.
–If there is only one candidate remaining, the Uncontested Elections procedures outlined in uncontested-elections shall apply.
–Repeat steps 2–6 until one winner is declared.
–The number of first‐choice votes for each candidate is counted.
–If two or more candidates have each received more than 50% of the vote, the top two candidates are declared the winners, and the procedure is complete.
–In the event that there is only one candidate with more than 50% of the vote, or zero candidates with more than 50% of the vote, the candidate who received the lowest number of first choice votes is dropped from the running.
–In the event that two or more candidates are tied in receiving the lowest number of first-place votes, all tied candidates are dropped from the running, except in the case when this would reduce the remaining eligible candidates to one.
–In such a case, the candidate to be dropped will be the candidate with the lower rank on the National Executive ballot.
–Only one candidate will be dropped.
–On all ballots with the dropped candidate ranked as a first choice, the candidate ranked second on the ballot is treated as having been ranked first, unless the second choice candidate has already been dropped.
–In this case, the next choice will be counted as first, etc.
–The number of first choice votes for each candidate is counted again.
–If only one candidate receives more than 50% of the vote when there are two candidates remaining, that person is elected, and the remaining National Councillor position is reopened. If no candidates receive more than 50% of the vote when there are two candidates remaining, no one is elected, and the elections are held again.
–Repeat steps 2–6 until two winners are declared.
(b)Where two or more positions are to be filled, the positions shall be filled sequentially using IRV. Following the election or nomination of each candidate, that candidate shall be removed from the remaining ballots, and the process shall be repeated until all positions have been filled.
i.A candidate must obtain more than 50% of the votes to be declared elected or nominated, as the case may be.
(c)The National Executive shall submit a ranked list of candidates to the CRO to only be used in the event of a tie.

Proposed Constitution

14Amendments

14.1
–The Constitution of the Federation may be repealed or amended by resolution at a General Meeting where no less than two thirds (2/3) active members present must agree.
–Amendments to this constitution that are simply corrective measures to ensure accurate translation and grammatical structure may be passed by the Board with a two thirds (2/3) majority, provided these amendments do not change the concept or spirit of the point being amended.
–The Board may prescribe rules and regulations consistent with this Constitution relating to the management and operation of the Federation as they deem expedient.
Subject to the Articles, the Board may, by Resolution, make, amend or repeal any provisions of this Constitution that regulate the activities or affairs of the CFES, except in respect of matters referred to in subsection 197(1) of the Act.
RewrittenConstitution §16.3 Temporary Amendments, cl. 1Constitution §16.1 Substantive Amendments, cl. 1Constitution §16.2 Grammatical Amendments, cl. 1
14.2
–The Constitution of the Federation may be repealed or amended by resolution at a General Meeting where no less than two thirds (2/3) active members present must agree.
–The rules and regulations shall have force and effect only until the next General Meeting when they shall be confirmed.
–If the rules and regulation fail to be confirmed, they shall at and from that time cease to have any force and effect.
Any such amendment or repeal shall be effective from the date of the Board Resolution until the next General Meeting where it may be confirmed, rejected or amended by the Members by Resolution.
(a)If the amendment or repeal is confirmed or confirmed as amended by the Members, it remains effective in the form in which it was confirmed.
(b)The amendment or repeal ceases to have effect if it is not submitted to the Members at the next General Meeting or if it is rejected by the Members at the General Meeting.
(c)If an amendment or a repeal ceases to have effect, a subsequent Board resolution that has substantially the same purpose or effect is not effective until it is confirmed, or confirmed as amended, by the Members at a General Meeting.
(d)This does not apply to any amendment that requires a Special Resolution of the Members under subsection 197(1) (fundamental change) of the Act because such amendments or repeals are only effective when confirmed by the Members.
